content.title: Mariners Game Information — March 26 at San Diego (Exhibition)
content.text: Press enter or click to view image in full sizeAS YOU MAY KNOW…the Mariners begin the 2024 regular season in 2 days, with a 7:10 p.m. matchup against the Boston Red Sox set for Thursday, March 28, but…DID YOU KNOW?…that tickets still remain for each of the 7 games on the Mariners opening homestand at T-Mobile Park?…every night of the Cleveland series (4/1–4/3) is a Value Game with tickets starting as low as $10, and each night is also a Julio Rodríguez “No Fly Zone” Bobblehead Night (first 10,000 fans)…more information is available at Mariners.com/tickets.TODAY’S TILT…the Mariners and Padres meet for their second of 2 exhibition matchups at Petco Park before the regular season gets underway…Seattle opens the 2024 regular season with a 4-game series against the Boston Red Sox at T-Mobile Park, beginning Thursday, March 28 on Opening Day with a 7:10 pm PT first pitch.ON THE AIR…today’s game will be broadcast live on Seattle Sports (710 AM) with Rick Rizzs and Gary Hill Jr. on the call…the game will also be televised live on ROOT Sports via bonus coverage.Get Mariners PR’s stories in your inboxJoin Medium for free to get updates from this writer.Remember me for faster sign inLAST NIGHT’S GAME…the Mariners defeated the Padres by a 4–1 score in last night’s exhibition contest at Petco Park…right-hander Bryce Miller made his final start before the regular season, getting the victory while tossing 4.0 innings of one-run ball…Jorge Polanco supplied a 2-run double for the Mariners in the top of the third inning off San Diego starter Dylan Cease, while Ty France went 3-for-3 with a run batted in against his former team, the Padres…in total, Seattle totaled 8 hits compared to San Diego’s 3…Seattle relievers Cody Bolton, Brett de Geus, Andrés Muñoz, Gabe Speier, Ryne Stanek and Troy Taylor stifled San Diego hitters all game long, combining for 5.0 scoreless innings out of the bullpen with just 2 hits allowed, no walks and 3 strikeouts.OPENING HOMESTAND…the Mariners return home to begin the 2024 regular season on Thursday, March 28 vs. the Boston Red Sox, the first of a season-opening 7-game homestand…tickets remain for all 7 home games vs. the Boston Red Sox (March 28–31) and Cleveland Guardians (April 1–3)…every night of the Guardians series is a Value Game with tickets starting as low as $10, and each night is also a Julio Rodríguez “No Fly Zone” Bobblehead Night (first 10,000 fans)…more information is available at Mariners.com/tickets.FUN AT T-MOBILE PARK IN APRIL…the Mariners will open the 2024 regular season at T-Mobile Park, with Opening Day against the Boston Red Sox on March 28…promotions during the first month of the season include 3 consecutive Julio Rodríguez “No Fly Zone” Bobblehead Nights from April 1–3 vs. Cleveland, with bobbleheads going to the first 10,000 fans each game…“Mariners Hoodie Night” on April 12 vs. the Cubs…“Salute To Armed Forces Night — Mariners Cap” on April 13 vs. the Cubs…3 consecutive Ken Griffey Jr. “Home Run Robbery” Bobblehead Nights from April 15–17 vs. Cincinnati…other promotions include “Mariners Turn Ahead The Clock Jersey Night” on April 26 vs. Arizona, “90s Night — Mariners Neon Hat Night” on April 27 vs. Arizona, 2 Little League Days (April 14 & 28), Jackie Robinson Day on April 15 and “Bark at the Park” on April 29 vs. Atlanta.SPRING POWERS…Jorge Polanco hit .436 (17x39) with 10 runs, 4 doubles, 3 home runs and 15 RBI with a 1.280 OPS in 16 Cactus League games, with his 15 RBI tied for 3rd-most in the Cactus League…Mitch Haniger hit .429 (15x35) with 8 runs, 3 doubles, 5 homers, 7 RBI and a 1.430 OPS…Julio Rodríguez hit .414 (12x29) with 9 runs, 3 doubles, 1 homer, 5 RBI and 7 walks with a 1.149 OPS…Dylan Moore batted .382 (13x34) with 7 runs, 2 doubles, 1 homer, 7 RBI, 10 walks and a 1.052 OPS…Ryan Bliss hit .333 (12x36) with 8 runs, 3 doubles, 1 homer, 9 RBI and an .868 OPS…Ty France also hit .333 (13x39), with 4 doubles, 6 RBI, 6 walks, 4 strikeouts and an .862 OPS…J.P. Crawford hit .325 (13x40), top prospects Cole Young (.333/8x24), Tyler Locklear (.320/8x25) and Jonatan Clase (.321/9x28) also hit above-.300 in spring action…Dominic Canzone registered 4 home runs and 11 RBI with a 1.109 OPS…Cal Raleigh had 4 homers and 13 RBI with a 1.089 OPS.READY TO “ROCK” OPENING DAY…Luis Castillo was named the Mariners Opening Day starter and is set to make his 4th career and 2nd consecutive Opening Day start…“La Piedra” is set to become the 10th pitcher in Mariners history to make multiple Opening Day starts with the club…in last year’s season-opener, Castillo blanked the Guardians on 1 hit over 6.0 innings, becoming the first pitcher in franchise history to hold the opponent scoreless over at least 6.0 innings while allowing 1-or-fewer hits.
